subject: French
examFormat: The syllabus aims to prepare candidates for the UTME and tests their general ability to assess written comprehension in French; apply the principles governing the structure and use of written French; identify how French sounds work in speech production; and examine the culture of Francophone West Africa and France in relation (where possible) to the home country. No exam format is stated.
recommendedTexts: Adeleke, J. — A Short French Grammar, 5th Edition (Badagry: Success Printers, 2018)
Adeniyi, E. A. — Contes Nigerians II, Revised Edition (Ilorin: Adek Graphic Productions, 2006)
Ajiboye, T. — Companion to French Grammar, 4th Edition (Ibadan: Cleavoketa Books, 2014)
Ajiboye, T. — Nouvel Horizon, Book 4, New Revised Edition (Ibadan: Bounty Press, 2012)
Hatier — Le Nouveau Bescherelle: L'Art de Conjuguer (Ibadan: Spectrum Books Ltd, 1980)
Maice, G. et Merlo, G. — Grammaire progressive du français, Niveau intermédiaire (Paris: Clé International, 1998)
Mazauric, C. et Sirejols, E. — On y va! Book 3 (Ibadan: Spectrum Books Ltd, 2006)
Ojo, S. A. — A Comprehensive Revision Handbook of French Grammar (Ibadan: Agoro Publishing Company, 2000)
Ajiboye, T. — An Introduction to Practice in Oral French (Ibadan: Bounty Press, 2010)
Girod, R. and Grand-Clement, F. — Comment vivent les Français (Paris: Hachette, 1979)
Mbuko, L. — French Essays on Culture and Civilisation for Schools and Colleges (Ibadan: Bounty Press, 2000)

Any other relevant materials on French grammar; any other materials that emphasize oral practice; French newspapers, magazines, journals and documents on Francophone life; any good French/English or French dictionary

topics.name: Written Comprehension in French
objectives: deduce answers to questions on the content, intent and style of proposed texts
apply reasoning skills
topics.content: Texts on topics of general and emergent interest, e.g. love, life, death, politics, marriage, health, communication, child trafficking, cultism, travel, corruption, money-laundering, etc.

topics.name: Principles Governing the Structure and Use of Written French
objectives: identify what constitutes the basic structures of written French
use the principles governing the structure of written French to determine acceptability, e.g. to transform one form or class into another
apply the structure to convey diverse messages
apply communicative skills
topics.content: Set expressions include proverbs (e.g. tel père tel fils, petit à petit l'oiseau fait son nid), idioms (e.g. avoir une faim de loup, crier sur le toit, mourir de peur), conventional stretches (e.g. enchanté, c'est dommage, c'est formidable, stationnement interdit), common figures of speech (métaphore: Mon père est un lion; simile: Elle est maigre comme un clou; hyperbole: Il avait tellement faim qu'il a mangé toute une vache) and speech acts (e.g. proposer, conseiller, regretter, admirer, espérer, interroger, reprocher, s'accorder). Covers identification of basic form classes, assessment of vocabulary span, word order, basic language-structure processes, and the use of French in set expressions.

subtopics.name: Identification of Basic Form Classes
objectives: identify what constitutes the basic structures of written French
use the principles governing the structure of written French to determine acceptability

subtopics.name: Nouns (Noms)
objectives: identify nouns: simple/compound, singular/plural, masculine/feminine

subtopics.name: Pronouns (Pronoms)
objectives: identify personal, impersonal, demonstrative, possessive and relative pronouns

subtopics.name: Verbs (Verbes)
objectives: identify reflexive and non-reflexive verbs, and their moods and tenses

subtopics.name: Adjectives (Adjectifs)
objectives: identify qualifying, possessive, interrogative, demonstrative, indefinite (e.g. nul), numeral (e.g. dix) and ordinal (e.g. dixième) adjectives

subtopics.name: Adverbs (Adverbes)
objectives: identify common adverb forms: with -ment (e.g. lentement) and with préposition + noun (e.g. par avion, à cheval, en voiture, par bateau)
identify special forms (e.g. bien, vite, mal, mieux, le mieux, pire, le pis, ne...que)

identify adverb types: manner (e.g. debout, facilement), purpose, cause and consequence, concession, place (y, en, ici, là, là-haut, partout) and time (hier, aujourd'hui, avant-hier, après, demain, la veille)

subtopics.name: Prepositions (Prépositions)
objectives: identify simple prepositions (e.g. à, de, avec, avant, sur, dans) and compound prepositions (e.g. à côté de, au milieu de)

subtopics.name: Conjunctions (Conjonctions)
objectives: identify conjunctions of co-ordination (e.g. mais, ou, et, donc, car, cependant, ne...ni) and of subordination (e.g. afin que, quoique, à condition que, pour que, parce que)

subtopics.name: Articles (Articles)
objectives: identify definite, indefinite and partitive articles

subtopics.name: Contraction
objectives: use contractions, e.g. à + le = au, à + les = aux

subtopics.name: Assessment of Vocabulary Span
objectives: identify meaning of words
identify meaningful constructed sentences

subtopics.name: Importance of Word Order
objectives: use correct word order in affirmative, interrogative and imperative sentences and in passive voice formation

subtopics.name: Basic Processes in Language Structure
objectives: apply conjugation in all tenses except l'imparfait du subjonctif, le passé composé du subjonctif and le plus-que-parfait du subjonctif
apply negation (e.g. ne...pas, ne...plus, ne...rien, nul ne, ne...ni...ni, ne...personne, personne...ne, aucun...ne, rien ne...)
apply agreement (e.g. les beaux arts, il les a vues)
apply pluralisation (e.g. cheval/chevaux, beau/beaux, belle/belles)

apply derivation: adjective to adverb (lent-lentement), adjective to adjective (un-premier), adjective to noun (bon-bonté, riche-richesse), and degrees of comparison (plus...que, moins...que, aussi...que), including special forms (bon, meilleur, le meilleur, la meilleure, mauvais, pire, le pire)

subtopics.name: Use of French in Set Expressions
objectives: complete common proverbs and idioms in French
deduce the meaning of idioms and proverbs in French
make appropriate use of these special terms

topics.name: Workings of French Sounds
objectives: discriminate between French sounds
deduce meanings out of sound combinations
use the above to enhance effective communication
assess sound groupings in terms of how they are affected by such features as syllabification, liaison, e-caduc, pause, intonation, etc.
topics.content: Sound discrimination (e.g. tout/tu, fais/fée); letter-sound correspondence (e.g. ai-/e/, eau/o/); syllabification (e.g. con/tente/ment); liaison (e.g. trois animaux, des enfants); sense groups in reading (e.g. J'ai mal à la tête. J'ai mal/pas à la tête / mais au dos/.); faux amis (e.g. librairie/library, rester/to rest, blesser/to bless); identification of sounds to determine similarity (e.g. maison/saison, dents/don, fond/fonde).

topics.name: Culture and Civilization
objectives: identify the specific features of the culture of Francophone Africa and France: greetings, dressing, food, leisure, marriage, festival, art, profession etc.
compare these features with those of the home country (where possible)
apply reasoning skill
topics.content: Characteristics (aspects, similarities and differences) of the educational system, socio-economic life, political organization and cultural life of Francophone Africa and France, with reference (where possible) to the home country, i.e. Nigeria.
